question: Water levels in rivers are unusually low due to the heat and drought1. Low water levels are expected to occur more frequently in the future. It is precisely during periods of drought that demand for water is high. As upstream countries retain more water, the situation in downstream countries, such as the Netherlands, becomes even more acute2.

The water needs of different EU countries are set to increasingly come into conflict with one another. The integrated framework for European climate resilience and risk management offers opportunities to bolster international solidarity. 1.

How does the Commission safeguard the position of downstream countries during periods of water scarcity, and does the Commission agree that greater solidarity between Member States is needed to ensure the availability of water for downstream countries in the future?

Is the Commission prepared to promote agreements between Member States on solidarity in the event of unusually low water levels, and to incorporate the promotion of such agreements into the integrated framework for European climate resilience and risk management (ECRRM)3?
Does the Commission see any added value in strengthening the mandate of river commissions to promote cooperation in international river basins, including crossborder regional rivers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.8.2026) Solidarity and open cooperation are key in transboundary water management. Article 13 of the Water Framework Directive1 (WFD) requires Member States sharing an international river basin to coordinate their river basin management plans, including measures to address water abstraction and ensure enough water flows to achieve good ecological status.

Moreover, as Parties to the UN Economic Commission for Europe Water Convention2, Member States must ensure ‘exchange of information on existing and planned uses of water and related installations that are likely to cause transboundary impact’.

Article 12 of the WFD3 also allows a Member State to notify the Commission and the other Member States concerned if it faces a water management issue that it cannot resolve alone, and to propose recommendations for addressing it. The WFD does not specify which form the cooperation between Member States should take when addressing water scarcity.
In practice, Member States use a range of bilateral or multilateral agreements, which the Commission regularly assesses. However, low flows issues are not addressed consistently4.

In its recent assessment of the WFD implementation5, the Commission thus recommended Member States to improve transboundary cooperation, including in the context of the river commissions on quantitative aspects of water management through relevant international cooperation mechanisms and bodies.

The integrated framework for European climate resilience and risk management6, will help Member States and the EU strengthen preparedness for future climate conditions. This will be an important contribution to improving water resilience and security, including across shared river basins and in other transboundary contexts.
1 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a

framework for Community action in the field of water policy, OJ L 327, 22.12.2000. 2 Convention on the Protection and use of Transboundary Watercourses and International Lakes. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:L_202600805. This article was recently amended and strengthened by making this cooperation mandatory.

4 An overview is available in the report ‘Assessment of the third River Basin Management Plans under the Water Framework Directive – Assessment of international cooperation under the Water Framework Directive – International River Basins’ (February 2025), available on CIRCABC: https://circabc.europa.eu/ui/group/9ab5926d-bed4-4322-9aa7-9964bbe8312d/library/3bb909f7-04c8-4e1e-9a37337a575239d8/details.

5 Report from the Commission to the Council and the European Parliament on the implementation of the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC) and the Floods Directive (2007/60/EC) – Third river basin management plans – Second flood risk management plans, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52025DC0002. 6 Scheduled for adoption in the fourth quarter of 2026.
